source.title: [Paper] All's Fair In Love And Love: Copy Suppression in GPT-2 Small
source.authors: CallumMcDougall; Arthur Conmy; Tom McGrath; Neel Nanda

record.file_problem: None; the complete post and comments are supplied.
record.tranche_reason: The post reports that copy suppression explains some, but not all, self-repair in the IOI task, refining the scope of a proposed mechanism.
record.gate_note: The reported 76.9% result and the CSPA-versus-mean-ablation KL comparison assess how well copy suppression describes L10H7's behavior, not self-repair itself, so they are not rows for these claim versions. The post also mentions qualitative experiments on self-repair without giving their detailed results.
record.test_reason: The post reports, in words only, that copy suppression (L10H7/L11H10 in GPT-2 Small) carries an important part, but not all, of self-repair in IOI. That is a result on V5's named-mechanism claim in a narrow task setting. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors call copy suppression an important part of self-repair in IOI, explaining some but not all of it, and say it helps resolve negative-head self-repair from the IOI paper. Separately, the unembedding direction did not explain self-repair well. They leave other forms of self-repair to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The post describes copy-suppression-preserving ablation and qualitative IOI self-repair experiments, rather than a direct reproduction of the original self-repair measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The self-repair discussion is centered on the IOI task; the post does not report a comparison across prompt sets or ablation types for this result.

fits_no_version.finding: Projecting L10H7's query-side residual onto predicted tokens' unembedding directions significantly harms performance. The unembedding direction also fails to explain self-repair well, so the head's query input is not fully captured by the unembedding directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Copy-suppression heads detect predicted tokens via latent features beyond the tokens' unembedding directions.

record.problems: The post gives only qualitative self-repair findings, without numerical effect sizes, uncertainty estimates, detailed intervention procedures, or stated controls for those experiments.
record.rows_left_out: The CSPA/mean-ablation KL comparison and the 76.9% figure describe how well copy suppression accounts for L10H7's behavior, rather than measuring self-repair; excluded from rows.

untested.parts: Layer-level compensation by later attention layers.
Late-MLP downregulation and its reduction after ablation.
Head-level self-repair on general text across model families and sizes.
Backup heads, final LayerNorm rescaling and anti-erasure neurons. Copy suppression's share of self-repair outside IOI and outside GPT-2 Small.
Self-repair under mean or resample ablation versus zero ablation.

missing.what: Weight-based (Q-composition) relationship between Name Mover Heads and self-repair heads: the name movers change how much the self-repair heads attend to names. This is a qualitative figure only.
Quantitative self-repair results (magnitudes of copy suppression's share of self-repair) are only in the linked paper (arXiv:2310.04625, Section 4.2), not in the post.

record.verdict_notes: This is a blog post summarising arXiv:2310.04625. The 76.9% figure and the CSPA-versus-mean-ablation KL results measure how much of L10H7's behaviour copy suppression explains, not self-repair, so excluding them from the rows is correct. Verdicts rest on qualitative statements in the post.

versions.untested_parts: Layer-level compensation by later attention layers.
Late-MLP counterbalancing and its change after earlier components are ablated.
Head ablations and compensation on the full distribution across model families and sizes.

The post discusses copy suppression as one contributor to self-repair, but does not test backup heads, copy-suppression contributions across models, final LayerNorm rescaling, or anti-erasure neurons as mechanisms.
Whether self-repair persists under on-distribution mean or resample ablations.
Whether ablation-based importance scores misstate component function.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 Small, IOI task, ablation of upstream copying heads
relationships.reason: R1: copy-suppression heads are described as 'an important part' of self-repair, with no reduction left to suppress once copying is ablated. The evidence is qualitative in the post.
relationships.display_finding: Copy-suppression heads contributed to self-repair because ablating upstream copying left no copying for them to suppress.
